plugins.name: Announcement Bar
plugins.description: One announcement bar at the top of every page: a short message, an optional link, four styles and an optional close button. Edited in the site settings, no third-party requests.
plugins.tagline: One clear announcement bar at the top of every page
plugins.longDescription:
Announcement Bar puts one short message at the very top of every published page: a sale, a holiday closing, a new product or an event. Type it in the site settings and it is live; empty the message and the bar is gone.

Add an optional link, such as "Shop the roast", to a page on your site or any https address. Pick a style that suits your theme: Quiet (dark), Loud (blue), Warm (orange) or your own colour, with text that switches between light and dark by itself to stay readable.

Let visitors close it if you like. A closed bar stays closed in that visitor's browser until you change the message, so a new announcement always gets seen.

It is small and respectful: a few lines of CSS, a tiny script only when closing is enabled, no fonts, images, tracking or third-party requests. The bar is a labelled region with a real, keyboard-focusable close button and escaped text.

It needs only the storage permission, for its settings. Without it, pages are served unchanged.

screenshots.caption: A warm announcement bar with a link above a live page
Close-up: message, link and a close button visitors can use
Message, link, style, colour and close option in the site settings

plugins.name: Breadcrumbs
plugins.description: A breadcrumb trail above the page content, built from the page address and your page titles, with BreadcrumbList structured data for search engines. Hidden on the home page.
plugins.tagline: A breadcrumb trail above every page, with structured data for Google.
plugins.longDescription:
Breadcrumbs shows visitors where they are with a small trail above the page content, like Home › Writing › This post. Every step but the last is a link, so going one level up is one click away. The home page never gets a trail.

The trail is built from the page address and your own page titles. A page at journal/spring-menu under a page called Journal reads Home › Journal › Our spring menu. When a step is not a published page, it is shown as plain text instead of a link that goes nowhere.

It also adds BreadcrumbList structured data, so search engines can show the trail in results instead of a bare address. When your site has a domain, the links in it are full URLs. If another plugin already added breadcrumb data, it leaves that alone.

It needs no setup. Out of the box you get plain dark teal links with a › between them. In the site settings you can rename Home, pick a chevron, slash, arrow or dot, switch to rounded pills, choose your own link colour, hide the current page from the trail, turn the structured data off, or skip pages by slug.

It is light and accessible. There is no script at all, no fonts and no third-party requests: about 1 KB of CSS. The trail is a nav landmark named Breadcrumb with an ordered list, the current page is marked for screen readers, separators are not read aloud, links have a visible focus ring, and the default colour passes WCAG AA on a light page. It is hidden when printing.

It asks for two permissions. Storage keeps its settings; refuse it and it runs with the defaults. Read pages lets it use your page titles and check which pages exist; refuse it and each step is named after its address, as plain text.

Good to know: Stride currently serves published pages at one-level addresses, so a trail has three or more steps only for pages whose slug has a slash in it.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a quiet trail above the article, built from the address and your page titles.
Close up: every step but the current page is a link, with a › between them.
Your own home name, arrow separators, rounded pills and your link colour.
Every option in the plugin's settings: home name, separator, style, colour, current page, structured data.

plugins.name: Celebrate
plugins.description: A burst of confetti on your thank-you pages, after an order, sign-up or booking, and on any link to #celebrate. Visitors who prefer less motion see none.
plugins.tagline: Confetti for your thank-you pages, after an order, sign-up or booking.
plugins.longDescription:
Celebrate adds a burst of confetti to the happy moments on your site: the thank-you page after an order, a sign-up or a booking, a welcome page, a launch. List the pages that should open with confetti, and any link that points to #celebrate gives a burst when it is clicked.

Pick confetti, hearts or stars, in party colours, gold, pastel or your own colour, and choose a cheerful burst or a proper party. It lasts three seconds, is drawn on a layer that never gets in the way of a click, and then disappears.

Visitors who ask their device for less motion see no animation at all. It is a little over a kilobyte of script, added only to the pages that use it.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it celebrates on pages called thanks, thank-you and bedankt.

screenshots.caption: The booking page opens with a burst of confetti.
The settings: which pages, shapes, colours and how much.

plugins.name: Cookie Consent
plugins.description: An accessible GDPR cookie banner in Dutch or English, with accept, reject and per-category settings. It remembers the choice and tells other scripts through a data attribute and a DOM event.
plugins.tagline: An accessible GDPR cookie banner in Dutch or English, with no third parties
plugins.longDescription:
Cookie Consent adds a clean, accessible cookie banner to every published page. Visitors can accept everything, reject everything with one equally prominent click, or open the settings and choose per category: necessary, analytics and marketing.

The banner speaks the page's language: Dutch pages get Dutch text, all others English. Write your own text for either language, link your privacy policy, pick a floating card or a full-width bar, and set the background, text and button colours. Button text stays readable on any colour you choose.

The choice is remembered for 180 days in a first-party cookie, so returning visitors never see the banner flash. A small Cookie settings button, or any element with data-cookie-settings, lets visitors change their mind.

Other scripts can wait for consent: the html element carries data-cookie-consent (for example "necessary analytics"), a stride:consent event fires on document with the choice, and window.StrideConsent offers get() and open().

Everything is inline and about 4 KB. No external requests, no tracking of its own. It needs only the storage permission for its settings, and still shows its default banner if that permission is refused.

screenshots.caption: A floating card on a live page, with Accept all and Reject all given equal weight
Settings lets visitors choose analytics and marketing cookies one by one
Text, privacy link, layout and colours are set from the site settings
On a Dutch page the banner speaks Dutch; here as a light full-width bar

plugins.name: Copy Code
plugins.description: A copy button on every code block, with Copied feedback, a language label and optional line numbers. Clean CSS, no highlighting library, no third-party requests.
plugins.tagline: A copy button on every code block, with a language label and line numbers.
plugins.longDescription:
Copy Code puts a small toolbar on every code block on your site: the language on the left and a Copy button on the right. One click copies the code, and the button says Copied with a check mark so visitors know it worked.

It works with Stride's text blocks. Write your code between two lines of three backticks, with the language after the first, like ```bash, and it is published as a real code block. Code blocks from your theme or another plugin get the button too.

It needs no setup. Out of the box you get a clean dark code block with a language label. In the site settings you can switch to a clean light style, or keep your theme's own style and only add the button. You can turn on line numbers, change the button text for a site in another language, or skip pages by slug.

It is built to be light. There is no highlighting library, no web font and no third-party request: a few kilobytes of inline CSS and JavaScript, and only on pages that have code.

It is accessible by default. The button is a real button with a visible label and focus ring, and screen readers hear Copied. Line numbers are never read out or copied. If the browser blocks the clipboard, the code is selected and the button says which keys to press. Without JavaScript, visitors see the plain code block.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: clean dark code blocks with the language and a Copy button that says Copied.
Close up: the clean light style with line numbers, which are never copied.
Every option in Settings: style, language label, line numbers, button text and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Countdown Banner
plugins.description: A bar that counts down the days, hours and minutes to your sale, launch or order deadline, with a button, and hides itself when the time is up.
plugins.tagline: Count down to your sale, launch or order deadline, then step aside.
plugins.longDescription:
Countdown Banner shows a bar that counts down the days, hours, minutes and seconds to a moment you choose: the end of a sale, a product launch, the last day to order before the holidays. Add a button, such as Shop the sale, and pick a colour; the text colour is chosen for you so it stays readable.

Put it at the top of every page, or let it float at the bottom of the screen. The words are available in English, Dutch, German and French. Set the time in your own time zone, and every visitor sees the right countdown wherever they are, summer time included.

When the time is up the bar hides itself, or shows a closing message such as The sale has ended. The clock runs in the visitor's browser, so it stays right without publishing again. Without JavaScript, visitors still see the message and the date it ends.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep the countdown. You can skip pages, such as your checkout.

screenshots.caption: A countdown bar at the top of every page, with a button to the sale.
Floating at the bottom of the screen, here in Dutch on a phone.
The settings: message, end time, time zone, button, language, position and colour.

plugins.name: Custom Code
plugins.description: Adds your own code to the head or body of every page: analytics, a verification tag, a chat widget or a font. Choose which pages get it. No theme edits needed.
plugins.tagline: Add analytics, verification tags and widgets to every page. No theme edits.
plugins.longDescription:
Custom Code puts your own snippets into the published pages of your site: in the head, right after the opening body tag, or at the end of the body. It is the easy way to add a privacy-friendly analytics script, a search engine verification tag, a web font, a tag manager or a chat widget.

Choose which pages get the code: every page, only the pages you list, or every page except those. A * at the end of an address covers every page under it, so blog/* means all your posts under blog.

Your code is inserted exactly as you paste it, and each snippet is labelled in the page source, so you always know where it came from. Before saving, the plugin checks for the mistakes that break a page: an unclosed script tag, a whole page pasted in by accident, or code that is too long.

Only paste code from people you trust: it runs for every visitor. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your snippets. Changes apply to a page the next time it is published.

screenshots.caption: Snippets land exactly where they belong, and each one is labelled in the page source.
The settings: code for the head and the body, and which pages get it.

plugins.name: Dark Mode Toggle
plugins.description: A light and dark switch for visitors. Follows the device setting, remembers the choice and never flashes on load. The dark colours are derived from your site's own colours.
plugins.tagline: A light and dark switch that follows the device and never flashes.
plugins.longDescription:
Dark Mode Toggle gives every page of your site a dark version and a small switch for visitors. Before anyone chooses, pages simply follow the light or dark setting of the visitor's device. One click on the switch changes it, and the choice is remembered on every page and every visit.

There is nothing to design. The dark colours are worked out from your own design colours when a page is published: your lightest colour becomes a deep background, your darkest becomes the text, and everything in between follows, so text stays as readable as it was and your hues stay recognisable. Want more control? Pick your own dark background and text colour, or override single colours by name.

There is no flash of white when a page loads in dark mode: a one-line script in the page head puts the remembered choice back before anything is drawn. Form controls and scrollbars switch with the page.

The switch is a real button with an accessible name, a pressed state screen readers announce, a large target and a visible focus ring. Put it floating in a corner or at the end of your header menu. It only appears once its script has run, so visitors without JavaScript never see a button that does nothing. It is hidden when printing.

It is light: no third-party requests, fonts or images, about 2.5 KB in total. The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: the dark version is derived from your own colours and follows the device.
Close up: the switch at the end of the header menu, light and dark. The choice is remembered.
The settings: when to start dark, where the switch goes, your own dark colours and overrides.

plugins.name: External Links
plugins.description: Opens links to other sites in a new tab, adds a small arrow so readers know they are leaving, and sets noopener and optional nofollow for you. No JavaScript.
plugins.tagline: Links to other sites open in a new tab, safely, with a small arrow.
plugins.longDescription:
External Links takes care of every link on your site that points to another website. It opens them in a new tab, so visitors do not lose your page, and adds rel="noopener noreferrer" so the other site cannot reach back into yours.

A small arrow after the link shows readers they are about to leave, and screen readers hear "opens in a new tab". You can also ask search engines not to follow the links (nofollow), or mark them as paid or affiliate links (sponsored).

Your own pages are never touched: links within your site are left as they are, and the plugin picks up your site's domain when you publish. You can also list your other domains, such as a separate shop, so they count as your own. Links you already set to open in a certain way keep that, and domains you name, such as youtube.com, are left completely alone.

Everything happens once, when a page is published: there is no JavaScript on your pages. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: A reading list where every outside link gets a small arrow and opens in a new tab.
What changes in the page: new tab, noopener, nofollow and a hidden note for screen readers.
The settings: new tab, arrow, nofollow or sponsored, and your other domains.

plugins.name: Glossary
plugins.description: Explain your jargon where it appears. Terms you list get a dotted underline, and pointing at or tapping one shows what it means. No other setup.
plugins.tagline: Explain jargon where it appears: dotted underlines that show a definition.
plugins.longDescription:
Glossary explains the words your visitors might not know, right where they read them. List your terms once, each with a short explanation, and they get a dotted underline in your pages. Pointing at one, tapping it or tabbing to it shows the explanation in a small bubble.

It only touches running text. Headings, links, buttons, code, the menu, header and footer are left exactly as they are, and so is anything inside a tag. By default only the first mention of each term on a page is marked, so a page does not turn into a sea of underlines; you can mark every mention if you prefer.

Terms can have other spellings, like "SEO | search engine optimisation", and the longest match wins. The bubbles work with a mouse, a finger and the keyboard, close with Escape, and flip below the word when there is no room above.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your terms.

screenshots.caption: A menu that explains itself: tap or point at sourdough to see what it means.
The settings: one term per line, then choose how often to mark it and the colour.

plugins.name: Heading Anchors
plugins.description: A small # link beside every section heading that appears on hover or focus. One click copies a link straight to that section and scrolls to it smoothly. Stable ids from the heading text.
plugins.tagline: A # link beside every heading. Click to copy a link to that section.
plugins.longDescription:
Heading Anchors puts a small # beside every section heading on your pages. It stays out of the way until a reader points at the heading or tabs to it. One click scrolls smoothly to that section, puts it in the address bar and copies the link, with a short "Link copied" message. It is made for docs, guides and long articles that people want to share a specific part of.

It needs no setup. Out of the box H2 and H3 headings get a blue # after the text. Headings without an id get a stable one made from their text, so "Choosing your paper" becomes #choosing-your-paper, and links keep working when you publish again. The ids match the ones Table of Contents makes, and headings that already have an id keep it.

In the site settings you can link only H2 headings or go down to H4, pick a chain link icon or a section sign instead of #, move the symbol into the margin before the heading, choose your own colour, write your own copied message, turn copying off, or skip pages by slug.

It is accessible by default. Every symbol is a real link with a name like "Link to section: Choosing your paper", so it works without JavaScript and with screen readers. It shows on keyboard focus with a visible focus ring, and faintly on touch screens, which have no hover. The copied message is announced politely, smooth scrolling respects reduced motion, and sticky headers do not cover the section you land on.

It is light: about 2 KB of inline CSS and JavaScript, no third-party requests, fonts or images. The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a # appears beside the heading you point at, and one click copies its link.
Close up: the link scrolls smoothly to the section and confirms the copy with a short message.
A chain link icon in the margin, in your own colour, with your own copied message.
Every option in the plugin's settings: headings, symbol, position, colour, copying and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Image Lightbox
plugins.description: Lets visitors click an image to see it large, with the caption underneath and arrows to browse every image on the page. Works with the keyboard and on phones.
plugins.tagline: Click any image to see it large, with captions, arrows and swipe.
plugins.longDescription:
Image Lightbox lets visitors click an image on your site to see it big, on a dark or light background, with its description as a caption. Arrows, the arrow keys and a swipe on a phone step through the other images on the page, with a counter such as 2 / 4.

It is built on the browser's own dialog, so it works with the keyboard and with screen readers: images that can be enlarged are announced as buttons, Escape closes the viewer, and focus returns to the image you came from. Animations are left out for visitors who ask their device for less motion.

It is careful about what it touches. By default only images shown smaller than they really are can be enlarged, so small icons and decorations are left alone. Images inside a link, the header, the menu or the footer never open, so logos and buttons keep working. You can skip pages, such as your shop.

No libraries and nothing loaded from elsewhere: a small inline script and stylesheet, added only to pages that have images. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it simply uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Click an image and it opens large, with its caption and arrows to the next one.
A light background suits a bright, airy site. The counter shows where you are.
On phones, swipe to the next image and tap to close.
The settings: which images, captions, arrows, background and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Instant Pages
plugins.description: Makes clicking around your site feel instant: pages start loading while a visitor points at a link, and fade smoothly into each other. No scripts.
plugins.tagline: Pages load while visitors point at a link, and fade in smoothly.
plugins.longDescription:
Instant Pages makes moving around your site feel instant. When a visitor rests the pointer on a link, the browser quietly prepares that page; when they click, it is already there. Pages then fade into each other instead of flashing white.

It uses two features built into modern browsers, Speculation Rules and View Transitions, declared in two small tags. No script of ours runs and nothing is sent to anyone. Browsers without these features simply work as before.

It is careful. Addresses that do something when visited, such as signing out, checkout, the admin and the API, are never loaded early, and neither are links that open in a new tab, download a file or carry a search query. You can add your own addresses to that list, and choose to start loading only when a link is pressed, to save data.

Visitors who ask their device for less motion get a plain change between pages. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Point, prepare, click: the next page is ready before the visitor clicks.
The settings: when to load, how much, the change between pages and what to skip.

plugins.name: Last Updated
plugins.description: Shows "Last updated on 27 September 2026" on pages and posts, in Dutch or English to match the page. The date is the day the page was last published with new edits, taken from Stride's own records.
plugins.tagline: Shows when each page last changed, in Dutch or English, under the title.
plugins.longDescription:
Last Updated adds one quiet line to your pages and posts: "Last updated on 27 September 2026". Readers see at a glance that a guide, price list or article is still current, and you never have to type a date by hand again.

The language follows the page. Dutch pages read "Laatst bijgewerkt op 27 september 2026", every other page gets English. The date is recorded when a page is published with new edits, so re-publishing the whole site does not make every page look freshly updated. Right after installing, publish the site once and every page gets its date.

In Site settings you can put the line under the title or at the end of the content, choose a long, short or numeric date, write your own label and list pages that should never show a date. The home page is skipped by default.

The line is plain, accessible HTML with a real <time> element. It inherits your theme's font and colour, adds about 450 bytes of inline CSS and a small icon that screen readers skip. No JavaScript and no third-party requests.

It asks for storage, to keep its settings and the dates, and read-pages, to read the list of pages when one is published: a plugin has no clock of its own, so the date comes from Stride's own records. It never reads page content. If either permission is refused, pages are simply left as they are.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a quiet date under the title of an article, in the theme's own font and colour.
Close-up: the date sits between the title and the byline, as a real <time> element.
Dutch pages get Dutch automatically: "Laatst bijgewerkt op 27 september 2026".
Site settings: position, date format, your own label and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Listen
plugins.description: A Listen button under the title of long pages. The page is read aloud with the visitor's own device voices, highlighting each paragraph. Nothing is sent anywhere.
plugins.tagline: A Listen button that reads long pages aloud, highlighting each paragraph.
plugins.longDescription:
Listen puts a small "Listen · 4 min" button under the title of your longer pages. Press it and the page is read aloud, paragraph by paragraph, with the paragraph being read highlighted and kept in view. Pause, carry on, stop, or change the speed.

It uses the voices built into your visitor's phone or computer, so there is no service to pay for and nothing is sent anywhere. The button only appears when the device has a voice for the language of the page, so nobody gets English read in a French accent.

It reads what matters: headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes in the main part of the page, not the menu, header or footer. Long sentences are spoken in short pieces, which keeps some browsers from stopping halfway.

Choose how long a page must be before it gets the button, and which pages to skip. The button colour and language are yours to set. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Reading the story page aloud: the paragraph being read is highlighted and kept in view.
The settings: which pages get the button, highlighting, colour and language.

plugins.name: Lite Video
plugins.description: YouTube and Vimeo videos appear as a light poster with a play button. The real player, from youtube-nocookie.com or Vimeo, loads only when a visitor presses play.
plugins.tagline: YouTube and Vimeo videos that load only when a visitor presses play.
plugins.longDescription:
Lite Video makes the videos on your pages lighter and more private.

A YouTube or Vimeo player normally loads the moment a page opens: about a megabyte of script, fonts and tracking, for every visitor, whether they watch or not. Lite Video puts a poster in its place instead, drawn by the page itself: the video's title and a round play button. Nothing is fetched from YouTube or Vimeo until somebody presses play, so there is nothing to ask consent for. One press loads the real player and starts the video straight away.

It works on its own. Every YouTube and Vimeo video you add is handled, with no codes to type. YouTube videos play from youtube-nocookie.com, which sets no cookies until the video plays. A short line on the poster says where the video comes from.

You can pick the play button colour, hide the note, and let the plugin remember a visitor's choice in their own browser, so players load straight away on their next visit. If you want the video's own picture as the poster, you can turn on YouTube thumbnails, with a clear note that YouTube then sees each visitor. Both are off by default.

It is accessible and tiny: the play button is a real link with a label that names the video, so it works with a keyboard, a screen reader and even without JavaScript. The script is about a kilobyte.

It asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings. Without it, videos still load on click, with the default look.

screenshots.caption: A video on a page before anybody presses play: a poster, and nothing loaded from YouTube.
Close up: the video's title, a play button with a clear focus ring and a note on where it plays from.
One press later: the real player, from youtube-nocookie.com, already playing.
The settings: button colour, the note, optional thumbnails and remembering the visitor's choice.

plugins.name: Maintenance Mode
plugins.description: Shows visitors a polished coming-soon or maintenance page while you build, with an optional launch countdown and contact line. Signed-in editors still see the real site.
plugins.tagline: A polished coming-soon page for visitors while editors see the real site
plugins.longDescription:
Maintenance Mode puts a clean, full-screen coming-soon or maintenance page in front of your site while you build it. Visitors see the placeholder; you and your editors, signed in to Stride, keep seeing the real pages, with a small badge reminding you that the curtain is up.

It works with zero configuration. Optionally add your site name, your own headline and message, a launch date with a live countdown, and a contact line. An e-mail address becomes a link. Choose a dark or light look and an accent colour; text keeps its contrast whatever you pick. Dutch pages get Dutch default text.

It fails closed: the page is hidden before any script runs, so visitors without JavaScript never see the site. A noindex tag keeps search engines from indexing the placeholder. The countdown is accessible, animation respects reduced motion, and nothing is loaded from third parties.

It needs only the storage permission, for its settings. Refuse it and the default maintenance page still shows. Note that this hides the site, it does not lock it: the real HTML is still in the page source.

screenshots.caption: Visitors see a dark coming-soon page with the launch date, a live countdown and a contact link
Signed-in editors keep seeing the real site, with a small reminder badge
The light maintenance look with a custom accent, on desktop and phone
Headline, message, launch date, contact line and look are set from the site settings

plugins.name: Privacy Map
plugins.description: An OpenStreetMap of your location that loads only after a visitor clicks Show map. Until then it is your address on a placeholder, and nothing is fetched from another site.
plugins.tagline: An OpenStreetMap that loads only when a visitor asks for it.
plugins.longDescription:
Privacy Map shows where you are without handing your visitors to a map company the moment they open a page.

Until somebody clicks Show map, the map is a placeholder drawn by the page itself: your place name, your address and a button. No iframe, image, script or font comes from another site, so there is nothing to ask consent for. One click loads the real OpenStreetMap, with your pin, zoom controls and the usual attribution. A short note under the button says what happens next.

Type [map] on any page where the map should go, or pick a page, such as contact, and the map is added at the end of it. Set the location by pasting a link from openstreetmap.org or coordinates like 52.3731, 4.8922, then choose a zoom and a height. The button takes a colour of your choice.

If you like, the plugin can remember a visitor's choice in their own browser, so maps show straight away on their next visit. It is off by default.

It is accessible and light: a real link that still leads to the map without JavaScript, a keyboard-friendly button with a visible focus ring, a labelled map frame, and well under a kilobyte of script.

It asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings. Without it no map is shown, because there is no location to show.

screenshots.caption: Before a click: your address on a placeholder, and nothing loaded from another site.
Close up: place name, address, a Show map button and a note on what it loads.
One click later: the real OpenStreetMap with your pin, on the same page.
The settings: place name, address, location, zoom, height and the page to add it to.

plugins.name: Mobile Action Bar
plugins.description: A bar at the bottom of the screen on phones with Call, Email, Directions and your own button, like Book a table. One tap for visitors, no JavaScript.
plugins.tagline: Call, email, directions and booking, one tap away on phones.
plugins.longDescription:
Mobile Action Bar adds a bar to the bottom of the screen for visitors on a phone, with the buttons a local business needs most: Call, Email, Directions and a main button of your own, such as Book a table or Order now.

Fill in only what you want to show. Your phone number becomes a tap-to-call button, your address opens in Google Maps, and your own button can point to any page. The labels come in English, Dutch, German and French, and your colour is used for the icons and the main button.

It is plain links and icons, with no JavaScript. The page gets a little space at the bottom so the bar never covers your content, and the bar respects the rounded corners and home indicator of modern phones. You can also show it on every screen, where it floats at the bottom like a small dock.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your details. You can skip pages, such as your checkout.

screenshots.caption: On a phone: call, email, directions and your own button, always within reach.
Shown on every screen, it floats at the bottom like a small dock. Here in Dutch.
The settings: phone, email, address, your own button, language, colour and screens.

plugins.name: Opening Hours
plugins.description: Shows your opening hours as a neat table and a live "Open now · closes at 17:00" badge. Type [opening-hours] or [open-now] on any page.
plugins.tagline: Your opening hours as a neat table, with a live Open now badge.
plugins.longDescription:
Opening Hours shows when you are open, the way visitors want to know it: a clear table for the week, today highlighted, and a badge that says Open now · closes at 17:00, or Closed now · opens tomorrow at 09:00.

Type [opening-hours] on any page for the table, or [open-now] for the badge alone, and publish. You can also show the badge or the table in the footer of every page.

Enter each day like 09:00-17:00, add a lunch break with a second range, or write closed. Choose your time zone, so the badge is right for visitors abroad too, and a language for the day names: English, Dutch, German or French. A short note, such as Closed on public holidays, goes under the table.

The table is plain HTML and works without JavaScript. Whether you are open right now is worked out when a visitor looks, not when the page was published, by a few hundred bytes of script. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your hours.

screenshots.caption: A visit page with the week's hours, today highlighted, and the Open now badge.
In Dutch on a phone, on a Sunday evening: closed, and when you open again.
The settings: hours for each day, a note, your time zone, language and footer.

plugins.name: Print Friendly
plugins.description: A clean print stylesheet for every page: navigation, footers and banners hidden, link addresses shown, sensible page breaks. Plus an optional Print this page button.
plugins.tagline: Pages that print cleanly: no menus or banners, full link addresses, tidy breaks.
plugins.longDescription:
Print Friendly gives every page a proper print stylesheet, so a visitor who prints a recipe, a guide or an article, or saves it as a PDF, gets the content and nothing else. Navigation, the footer, sidebars, cookie and consent banners, dialogs, forms and embedded video are left off the paper. Text prints black on white, backgrounds and shadows are dropped to save ink, and a sticky header no longer covers the first lines of every page.

Links stay useful on paper. The full address is printed after each link, including links to your own pages, so a reader can still find them. Links whose text already is the address, email and phone links, and image links are left alone. Headings stay with the text that follows them, images, tables, code and quotes do not split across pages, table headers repeat, and closed details sections open for printing.

It needs no setup and changes nothing on screen. In the site settings you can turn off link addresses, hide more parts of your pages by CSS selector, skip pages by slug, and add a Print this page button after the content or in the corner, with your own label.

It is light and accessible. About 2 KB of inline CSS and a few hundred bytes of script, with no third-party requests. The button is a real button with a printer icon, a visible label, a 44 px target and a focus ring; it only appears once its script is running, and it never prints itself.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and pages still print cleanly with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: the menu, footer and background stay on screen; the paper gets the article.
Close up on paper: every link is followed by its full address, including links to your own pages.
The optional Print this page button after the content, with a visible focus ring.
Every option in Settings: link addresses, extra parts to hide, the button, its text and position, pages to skip.

plugins.name: Promo Popup
plugins.description: One friendly popup for a sale, a newsletter or an event. Show it after a few seconds, on scroll or when someone is about to leave, and not again for days.
plugins.tagline: One friendly popup for a sale or newsletter. Never pushy.
plugins.longDescription:
Promo Popup shows one popup to your visitors: a sale, a newsletter, a workshop, a new product. Give it a title, a short text, an optional image and a button, and choose when it appears: after a few seconds, after scrolling down the page, or when a visitor is about to leave.

It is polite by design. Each visitor sees it once, and then not again for as many days as you choose, or only once per visit, or only ever once. Change the text and it counts as a new popup, shown again. It can sit in the middle of the screen or slide in small in a corner, and you can keep it off pages such as your checkout.

It uses the browser's own dialog, so Escape, the close button and screen readers all work, and animations are left out for visitors who prefer less motion. Whether a visitor has seen it is remembered in their own browser; nothing is sent anywhere and nobody is tracked.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep the popup.

screenshots.caption: A workshop invitation with an image and a button, in the middle of the screen.
Or small in the corner, where it does not get in the way of reading.
The settings: text, image, button, when to show it, how often, look and pages.

plugins.name: QR Code
plugins.description: A QR code for every page: a button to show and download it, [qr-code] to place it on a page, and in the corner of printed pages. Made on your server.
plugins.tagline: A QR code for every page, for menus, flyers, posters and printed recipes.
plugins.longDescription:
QR Code makes a QR code for every page of your site. Visitors can open it from a small button to show the page to someone else or download it, you can place it on a page by typing [qr-code], and printed pages carry it in a corner, so a printed menu, flyer or recipe leads straight back to the page online.

The codes are drawn on your own server as sharp vector images. Nothing is fetched from a QR service, and no visitor is tracked. If you want to know how many people came from a scan, switch on "Add ?ref=qr" and look for it in your analytics.

The codes point to your site's address. Fill it in, or let the plugin pick up the address your site is published at once it has a domain. Without an address it shows nothing, rather than a code that goes nowhere.

The words come in English, Dutch, German and French. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings.

screenshots.caption: The QR code of the menu page, ready to scan or download.
Printed, every page carries its own code in the corner.
The settings: button, print, site address, scan tracking, colour and language.

plugins.name: Quote Share
plugins.description: Readers select a sentence and share it as a quote on X, Bluesky, WhatsApp or by email, or copy a link that opens your page with that sentence highlighted.
plugins.tagline: Select a sentence and share it as a quote. Links open with it highlighted.
plugins.longDescription:
Quote Share turns your best sentences into shareable quotes. When a reader selects text in an article, a small bar appears above it: share the quote on X, Bluesky or WhatsApp, send it by email, or copy it with a link.

The copied link is special: in browsers that support it, it opens your page scrolled to that very sentence, highlighted. It is a standard of the web (text fragments), so it needs nothing from you.

Nothing loads from X, Bluesky or anyone else until a reader clicks, there are no cookies and nobody is tracked. Choose which buttons to show, the colour of the bar and on which pages it appears; by default it skips short pages and the home page.

Button labels come in English, Dutch, German and French for screen readers. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Select a sentence and the bar appears: X, Bluesky, WhatsApp, email or copy with link.
The settings: which buttons, colour, language and where the bar appears.

plugins.name: Reading Progress
plugins.description: A thin reading progress bar at the top of long pages, plus an optional back-to-top button. Pure CSS scroll-driven animation with a tiny JavaScript fallback.
plugins.tagline: A slim reading progress bar and a back-to-top button for long pages.
plugins.longDescription:
Reading Progress puts a thin bar across the top of every long page that fills as the reader scrolls, so they always know how much is left. Once they are half a screen down, a round back-to-top button fades in the corner and takes them back up with one click.

It needs no setup. Out of the box you get a 3 px rose bar and a button in the bottom right. Short pages that barely scroll get no bar. In the site settings you can pick your own colour, make the bar thin, medium or bold, move the button to the left, turn the button off, or skip pages by slug.

It is built to be light. The bar runs on a native CSS scroll-driven animation, so modern browsers do not run any code on scroll. Older browsers get the same result from a tiny inline script. There are no third-party requests, fonts or images: about 2 KB in total.

It is accessible by default. The bar is decorative and hidden from screen readers. The button is a real link with an accessible name, a 44 px target and a visible focus ring. It picks a white or dark arrow to stay readable on your colour, scrolls smoothly only for visitors who have not asked for reduced motion, and is hidden when printing.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a slim rose bar at the top and a back-to-top button in the corner.
Close up: the bar tracks how far the reader is; the button fades in half a screen down.
Your colour, a bold 8 px bar and the button on the left.
Every option in Settings: colour, thickness, back-to-top button, its position and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Reading Time
plugins.description: Shows an estimated reading time, like "4 min read", under the first heading of every page, and keeps a per-page word count an editor can see in the site settings.
plugins.tagline: Shows readers how long a page takes, like "4 min read", under the title.
plugins.longDescription:
Reading Time counts the words on each page and shows an estimate like "4 min read" right under the first heading. Readers see at a glance how long a guide, article or case study will take before they start.

There is nothing to set up. With the default settings you get a small pill with a clock icon. It uses the page's own text colour, so it suits any theme. Only the prose in the article is counted: scripts, styles, navigation, footers and asides are skipped. The estimate is rounded up to whole minutes and is never less than one.

In Site settings you can set the reading speed (200 words a minute by default), change the label (for example to "minuten leestijd"), pick an accent colour, list pages to skip, such as home and contact, or switch to plain text that your theme styles itself. The panel also shows how many pages have been counted and which one is the longest.

The published page gets no JavaScript and makes no third-party requests. The badge adds under 600 bytes of inline CSS, and its clock icon is hidden from screen readers, so assistive technology reads just "4 min read". The label you type is escaped before it goes into the page.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings and the per-page word counts. If you refuse it, every page still gets a reading time with the default settings.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a quiet "3 min read" badge under the title, in the page's own colours.
Close-up with a custom accent colour. The clock is decorative; screen readers hear just the time.
Every option in Site settings: speed, label, style, accent colour and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Related Pages
plugins.description: A Related reading block at the end of articles and posts, with the pages that share the most topics or title words. Cards or a list, built when the page is published.
plugins.tagline: Related reading at the end of every article, matched on topics and titles.
plugins.longDescription:
Related Pages ends your articles and posts with a short Related reading block: the pages on your site that have the most in common with the one just read. Readers who reach the end get somewhere to go next instead of a dead end.

It needs no setup. Out of the box it shows up to three cards, matched on the words in page titles and on the folder a page sits in, and it only appears on article-like pages, so your about and contact pages stay as they are. Pages with nothing in common are never suggested.

In the site settings you can switch to a compact list, show one to six pages, change the heading and accent colour, limit it to folders such as blog, skip pages, or show it on every page. Add topics per page and pages that share a topic are suggested first, with the topic shown above the title.

It is built to be light: about 2 KB of CSS, no JavaScript, no fonts, no images and no third-party requests. The block is an aside with a heading and a real list of links, it follows your theme's font and text colour, has a visible focus ring, respects reduced motion and is hidden when printing.

It asks for two permissions. Read pages lets it list your published pages and their titles; it reads nothing else and changes nothing. Storage keeps its settings. Refuse storage and it runs with the defaults; refuse read pages and it leaves your pages untouched. The block is built when a page is published, so publish the site again after adding new articles.

screenshots.caption: Related articles as cards at the end of the page, labelled by shared topic.
Close up: the shared topic above each title, and a violet border on hover.
The list style, with your own heading.
Every option in Settings: style, count, where it shows, folders, topics, colour and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Schema Markup
plugins.description: Adds JSON-LD structured data to every published page: your Organization or LocalBusiness (address, opening hours, phone), the WebSite, and a BlogPosting for posts, so Google can show rich results.
plugins.tagline: JSON-LD for your business, website and blog posts, ready for Google rich results
plugins.longDescription:
Schema Markup adds structured data to every published page, in the JSON-LD format Google, Bing and other search engines read. Visitors see nothing; search engines get a clear description of who you are and what each page is.

Describe your organization once in the site settings: name, logo, phone, email, address and social profiles. Choose Local business, Shop, Restaurant or Professional service to add opening hours such as "Mo-Fr 09:00-17:30" and a price range, which is what makes you eligible for local business results.

Every page also gets a WebSite entry. Blog posts, the pages whose address starts with blog or news, get a BlogPosting with the headline, description, social image, language, word count, author and publisher. The plugin takes these from the page itself, so there is nothing to fill in per post.

It works with no setup: the site name comes from your page titles and the site address from the canonical link. Every value is escaped, so nothing you type can break out of the script. It makes no external requests, adds no visible markup, and needs only the storage permission for its settings. If that permission is refused, it keeps working with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: A published blog post and the WebSite and BlogPosting data the plugin added to its head
A shop with address, opening hours, phone and social profiles, on every page

plugins.name: Scroll Reveal
plugins.description: Page content fades and slides into place as visitors scroll to it. Native CSS scroll-driven animations with a tiny fallback, and nothing moves for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
plugins.tagline: Content fades and slides into place as visitors scroll to it.
plugins.longDescription:
Scroll Reveal gives your pages a little life. As visitors scroll, headings, text, images and cards fade and slide gently into place, so a long page feels like it unfolds instead of just sitting there.

It needs no setup. Out of the box every block inside the page content fades up 40 px as it comes into view. Anything already on screen when the page opens stays exactly where it is, and the header, menu and footer are never touched. In the site settings you can pick fade up, fade in, slide in from the left or right, or zoom in; choose a small, medium or large distance; reveal whole sections at once instead of block by block; or skip pages by slug.

It is built to be light. Modern browsers run it as a native CSS scroll-driven animation, so no code runs while visitors scroll. Other browsers get the same look from a tiny inline script. There are no third-party requests, fonts or images: about 1.5 KB in total.

It respects your visitors. Anyone who has asked their device for reduced motion sees a normal page with nothing moving. Nothing is ever hidden from visitors without JavaScript, from screen readers or search engines, or when printing, and jumping straight to the end of a page never leaves content invisible.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: the work below the fold fades up into place as the visitor scrolls.
Close up: blocks already on screen stay put while the next one rises in.
Whole sections sliding in from the left, with a large distance.
Every option in the plugin's settings: effect, distance, what to reveal and pages to skip.

plugins.name: SEO Inspector
plugins.description: Checks every page when it is saved: title length, meta description, image alt text, headings, thin content and long URLs. Shows a 0-100 score and the warnings per page in the site settings.
plugins.tagline: A 0-100 SEO score and clear warnings for every page, checked on save.
plugins.longDescription:
SEO Inspector checks each page the moment it is saved and gives it a score from 0 to 100, with a plain list of what to fix.

It looks at what search engines and screen readers notice first: a missing or too short meta description, an SEO title that is too short or will be cut off in search results, images without alt text, pages with no h1 or more than one, skipped heading levels such as h2 followed by h4, thin content and long URLs.

All reports live in Site settings under SEO Inspector, worst page first, so you always know which page to fix next. The limits for thin content, title length and URL length are adjustable, and the defaults follow the usual rules of thumb.

It never changes a page and adds nothing to your published site: no scripts, no styles, no requests to anyone.

screenshots.caption: Every page with its score and warnings, worst first.
The panel in Site settings, with the thresholds you can adjust.

plugins.name: Site Search
plugins.description: A search box for your whole site. Visitors press ⌘K or click Search and find pages by title and text as they type. No outside service.
plugins.tagline: A search box for your whole site. Press ⌘K and find any page as you type.
plugins.longDescription:
Site Search adds a search box to your site. Visitors click Search in the page header, or press ⌘K, Ctrl+K or / anywhere, and find pages by title and text as they type. The matching words are marked, the arrow keys move through the results and Enter opens one.

There is no outside search service and nothing to set up. Every published page can be found by its title straight away, and a page's text joins the search the first time someone opens it. The search itself runs in the visitor's browser, so it is instant and works the same on every host.

It is careful with what it shows. Only published pages are in it, and text that only signed-in members may see is never searchable: a page with members-only blocks, in the page itself or in any component it uses, can be found by its title only.

It suits sites of up to a few hundred pages. The box speaks English, Dutch, German or French, following the language of the page by default. It needs two permissions: storage, to keep what each page contributes, and read pages, to know which pages are published.

screenshots.caption: Search on a restaurant site: results appear as you type, with the matching words marked.
On a phone the Search button sits in the header and the results fill the screen.
The settings: where the button goes, the shortcut, language, colour and pages to leave out.

plugins.name: Social Share
plugins.description: Adds share buttons for X, LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp, e-mail and copy link under your articles. Plain links and inline icons: no third-party scripts, no tracking.
plugins.tagline: Privacy-friendly share buttons under every article. No trackers.
plugins.longDescription:
Social Share adds a tidy row of share buttons under your articles: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp, e-mail and copy link.

Every button is a plain link with an inline icon. Nothing loads from Facebook, X or anyone else, so there are no third-party scripts, no cookies and no tracking. A reader's browser only talks to a network when the reader clicks its button.

It looks good straight away. Pick from four styles in the site settings: brand colours with labels, outlined, round brand icons, or minimal icons in your own accent colour. You can also change the heading, centre the row, switch off any network, and choose which pages show it, for example only pages under blog or news.

It is built to be accessible: descriptive labels for screen readers, a visible keyboard focus ring, a spoken "Link copied" confirmation, and no motion for readers who prefer reduced motion.

It asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still shows the default buttons.

screenshots.caption: Share buttons under a journal article, in the default brand-colour style.
Close-up: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp, e-mail and copy link, all plain links with inline icons.
All options in the site settings: heading, style, accent colour, alignment and networks.
The round-icon style, centred, with a custom heading.

plugins.name: Table of Contents
plugins.description: Builds a linked table of contents from the h2 and h3 headings of a page, gives every heading an anchor id, and puts it at the top of the article, boxed or as a sticky sidebar. No JavaScript.
plugins.tagline: A linked table of contents for long pages, built from your headings.
plugins.longDescription:
Table of Contents reads the h2 and h3 headings of a page, gives each one a clean anchor id and puts a linked, nested list of them at the top of the article, in the same column as your text. Readers can see what a long page covers and jump straight to the part they came for. Every heading also gets a shareable link, like /guide#what-a-drawing-is-for.

It needs no setup. Pages with at least three headings get a quiet box titled "On this page" in your site's own fonts and colours. Short pages, the header and the footer are left alone. Headings that already have an id keep it, and duplicate headings get unique anchors.

Prefer it out of the way? Switch to the sticky sidebar style. On wide screens the list stays in the left margin while the reader scrolls, and on smaller screens it falls back to the box. You can also number the sections, list only h2 headings, change the title, pick an accent colour, set the minimum number of headings and skip pages by slug.

The published page gets no JavaScript and makes no third-party requests. The links are plain anchors, the styling is about 1.5 KB of inline CSS, and smooth scrolling only happens for visitors who have not asked for reduced motion. The markup is an accessible nav landmark with a label and visible focus styles.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: an "On this page" box at the top of the article, in the site's own type.
Sections and subsections, nested, each one a plain anchor link. No JavaScript.
Sidebar style: numbered, with a custom accent, and sticky in the margin while you read.
Every option in Settings: headings, minimum count, title, style, numbering, accent and skipped pages.

plugins.name: WhatsApp Chat
plugins.description: A floating WhatsApp chat button with a preset message, left or right placement, your own colour and optional opening hours. Accessible, CSS-only animation, no third-party scripts.
plugins.tagline: A floating WhatsApp button with a preset message and opening hours
plugins.longDescription:
WhatsApp Chat adds a round WhatsApp button to the corner of every published page. One tap opens a chat with your number, with a message already typed that the visitor can still change.

Place it bottom right or bottom left, keep WhatsApp green or use your own colour, and add a short label such as "Questions? Chat with us". On phones the label hides itself so the button never covers your content.

Optionally show the button only during opening hours: choose the days, the times and your time zone, and visitors outside those hours simply see no button.

It is built to be light and respectful: a plain link to wa.me, no WhatsApp scripts, no tracking and no third-party requests. The pulse and hover animations are pure CSS and switch off for visitors who prefer reduced motion. The button is a real, keyboard-focusable link with a clear accessible name and a contrast-checked icon.

It needs only the storage permission, for its settings.

screenshots.caption: A WhatsApp button with a short label in the corner of a live page
On a phone the label steps aside and only the round button remains
Number, preset message, label, position, colour and hours in the site settings
